content:
Two things that I've been overdue on sharing:

  • iris-port This is the protocol I use to automatically port Rocq code to Lean, with the new /port-iris command. It has a relatively high success rate on Opus 4.8 medium (ime higher effort leads to worse outcomes). The first commit on the saved props PR is an example of what the plugin can do with no intervention in around 45 minutes, I'd consider this a pretty good first draft.

    Even if you're not porting a new file, once you install the plugin you can ask the "style critic" to make a pass over some code, and it will follow a range of suggestions derived from our chore: cleanup commits. After each session you can ask your agents to improve the plugin with what they learned by modifying the notes folder of the plugin. I'll gladly accept any PR of that sort.

  • aisandbox It's nothing super special, but this is the script I use to set up dockerfiles for my agents. I link it here because I will always assume you are using my iris-port script in auto-allow mode.

I want the number on the tracking website to be higher, so I'll probably clank out more of the low-hanging fruit in the repo over the next little bit.

Actually, to facilitate improving /port-iris, I added a step final to the workflow which will take suggestions, tweak the plugin, and write a script you can run outside of your container to PR the changes to port-iris itself (I am seriously staring into the AI abyss here). If you use port-iris, you should probably enable auto-updates.
